title: Multi-agent teams
summary: An orchestrator splits a big job across specialist agents, each with its own context.

steps.label: task
steps.title: A job too big for one context
payload: "Write a market report on AI note-taking apps"

steps.label: subtask
steps.title: Plan and delegate
steps.text: The orchestrator breaks the job into parts. Each sub-agent starts with a clean, focused context instead of one huge messy one.
payload: Briefs must be self-contained; sub-agents can't see the main chat.

steps.label: findings
steps.title: Return a summary, not everything
steps.text: The researcher might read 40 pages but returns a short report. That keeps the orchestrator's context small.
payload: Condensing is the main benefit of sub-agents.

steps.label: draft v1
steps.title: Independent review
steps.text: A separate agent with a critical brief catches mistakes the writer can't see in its own work.
payload: facts vs sources · missing competitors · claims without data

steps.label: 3 issues
steps.title: Feedback loops back
steps.text: The orchestrator decides whether to send it back for another round or accept it.
payload: price outdated · 1 uncited claim · missing summary

steps.label: final report
steps.title: Delivered
steps.text: Multi-agent setups use several times more tokens than one agent. Use them when the task really splits into independent parts.
